To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found an unexpected association between methotrexate pharmacokinetics and toxicity and polymorphisms of SLCO1B, a transporter not expressed in kidney.

we identified 38 (and 34) metabolites that are differentially excret ed by OAT1/O AT3 (and OAT3) carriers of the c. 388A>G or the c. 521T>C variant allele, half of them associated with methotre xate toxicity.

we identified endogenous metabolites that may mediate remote communication between the liver and kidney, through OATP1b1/OATs/OATP1b3, and explain the pharmacogenetic effect of SLCO1b1 polymorphisms on methotrexate pharmacokinetics and toxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and validation of an analytical method for the determination of the three main metabolites of methotrexate in urine samples by ultra‐performance liquid chromatography coupled to tandem mass spectrometry.
the development and evaluation of a new method of treatment of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) using the combination of hemodialysis and hemodiafiltration (HDF).

the study of the pharmacogenetic effect of the c.521T > C polymorphism of the SLC01B1 gene on the pharmacokinetics of methotrexate in patients with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) and acute myeloid leukaemia (AML).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OATP1‐mediated uptake of methotrexate in the liver is a key step in the elimination of methotrexates from plasma.
the pharmacogenetic associations between SLCO1B and methotrexate may be mediated by metabolites that are substrates of OATs, and the association is likely to be indirect.
the pharmacogenetic associations between methotrexate treatment and SLCO1B3 polymorphisms are mediated by metabolites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified new metabolites that could be used in the future as potential markers for the prediction of methotrexate‐related toxicity.
the association of SLCO1B and OATs polymorphisms with drug toxicity can be explained by the communication between OAT1/O3 and OATPs, and the metabolites‐mediated interactions between OATs and OATPs.
the SLCO1B 1 polymorphism may influence the excretion of endogenous substrates through OAT1/Oat1/Oat3 and OATPs in the kidney and liver, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the excretion profile is a reflection of the metabolic status of the organism.
the pharmacogenetics of methotrexate is complex, and the SLCO1B gene variants may not be the only ones responsible for the pharmacogenetic effect of methotrexat.
metabolites can be used to decipher the pharmacogenomics of transporter polymorphisms, which may help to identify new drug–transporter interactions.
